An independent exact re-expansion from the squared coordinate sums (python /workspace/independent_checks.py 4) checks both endpoint distances, the barycentric coefficient and 41 positive gap monomials in (s,k-s,q-k). All monomials contain k-s or s(q-k), with both of those monomials present, so the equality locus is exactly the two endpoints. Strict convexity excludes nonvertices. The proposed center is a strict convex mixture of the two orbit means; averaging squared distances gives R_q^2+||z-c_q||^2 for any alternative center z, proving uniqueness. RESULT.md:85 should say squared radius, not radius, is bounded below by this average; the preceding identity gives the intended result. The two unequal hub values identify (s,k) except at (0,0); precisely the first s leaves are indistinguishable. This yields the stated exact vertex count including q=2, and summing the factorial series yields the asymptotic contact fraction. No uploaded checker was executed.
